transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-04-22
- Start: 15:30 UTC (local times: SF 08:30, LON 16:30)
- End: 16:12 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Valora CTO), Liam O'Neil (Infra Lead), Sara Benton (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick check-in on contract extension + capacity uplift, gating criteria for EU+APAC region activation, brief technical ask for dedicated pool latency benchmarks, confirm procurement timeline and next pilot workshop.

Links referenced: pricing deck (https://redwood.example.com/decks/valora-pricing-v2), security whitepaper (https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-kms.pdf), benchmark sheet (https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/valora-uptick-2028.xlsx)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute, um so high level today is just alignment right? capacity, geo gates, procurement, and the bench- the benchmark follow-up.
[00:15] Priya: yeah thanks Maya. we got a lot of internal folks on standby, wanted to make sure we don't miss any blockers before the exec sign-off next week.
[00:28] Liam: hi all, Liam here, infra. our main ask is predictable p99 <-> region parity. last time we saw p99 jump when traffic spiked because of batching settings.
[00:41] Diego: yeah that makes sense, Diego from Redwood SE. so for the dedicated pool we can pin GPU capacity and enforce lower batch windows, that usually fixes p99; there are tradeoffs on cost.
[00:53] Sara: quick question from procurement: do you have one invoice for the Dedicated reserved or separate for Hosted overages? we need to map cost center.
[01:03] Maya: good Q Sara. normally reserved capacity is a single monthly commitment invoice, hosted usage over that is metered. for the uplift we can propose a blended take — I'll include both scenarios in the quote.
[01:18] Priya: can we also get the SLA for failover? if EU region goes, we want explicit failover to US-1 with a defined RTO/RPO or at least an automatic fallback policy.
[01:30] Diego: yes, we support smart routing and automated fallbacks to compatible model variants/regions. our typical canary + fallback policy will kick in; we can provide a written runbook. note there is an increase in token egress when cross-region fails over.
[01:49] Liam: that's the concern — egress and residency. for some flows we must keep data in EU. we need to understand private deployment / VPC options and KMS integration timelines.
[02:04] Maya: understood. Priya, last call you said you were open to a private VPC pilot for EU, right?
[02:12] Priya: yes, we want VPC with customer-managed KMS, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC2 evidence. can Redwood support HSM-backed keys?
[02:23] Diego: we support KMS + HSM integrations (customer-managed KMS). SOC2 docs are in the whitepaper I linked, we'll send the SOC audit package and architecture notes after the call.
[02:35] Sara: procurement will need those docs to advance the PO. also need a 60-day cancellation pt? standard legal questions.
[02:44] Maya: legal terms — we can propose a 12-month extension with a 60-day termination clause in the commercial amendment. I'll flag Legal to draft.
[02:57] Priya: on performance: Diego, would you do the dedicated-run bench with our sample workload? last time the KV cache warmed slowly and burst latency spiked.
[03:09] Diego: absolutely. we'll run a 100k-token back-to-back test and surface p50/p95/p99. two notes: if you want max throughput we recommend quantized model variant Q4_0 or Q5 for cost; but for strict quality keep FP16. there is a small repro of hallucination changes with quantization but usually minimal.
[03:29] Liam: okay, so we have two knobs: batch window and quantization. can you include cost delta for both in the sheet?
[03:38] Maya: yes, cost vs latency sensitivity will be in the spreadsheet. I'll include scenarios: hosted with auto-fallback, dedicated pinned pool, private VPC-onprem.
[03:49] Priya: about regions: once we hit the committed throughput threshold EU-1 -> we want automatic gate to enable APAC region. is that a manual gating or can Redwood automate when usage > threshold?
[04:02] Diego: we can do both. most customers prefer a staged gate: automatic flagging + ops approval. for you we can set a policy to auto-scale capacity and notify your infra for sign-off.
[04:13] Priya: we prefer ops approval for the first two activations. after that we can switch to auto.
[04:18] Maya: makes sense. procurement timeline? Sara?
[04:20] Sara: we are trying to get PO by the first week of May. need final commercial terms by next Wednesday, and SOC2 + KMS attestation to legal by Friday.
[04:30] Maya: ok i'll prioritize the security package and the commercial amendment. Diego will run the bench.
[04:34] [Short technical digression]
[04:36] Diego: slightly nerdy note — for long-context chat we keep KV cache pinned per session; for heavy reranking workloads we recommend a larger KV cache allocation and an instance with nvram-backed swap. that reduces repeated token compute.
[04:50] Liam: does Redwood have a recommended perf config for reranking plus retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)? last pilot we hit memory pressure.
[04:58] Diego: yes, RAG workloads benefit from larger KV + smaller batch windows; we also recommend continuous batching with prefix caching enabled. i'll paste the recommended config in the benchmark sheet.
[05:09] Priya: what about encryption in transit between model instances? need TLS + mutual auth.
[05:15] Diego: mutual TLS is supported in private deployments; for hosted we use TLS 1.2/1.3 with customer-side certs optional for peered VPC connections.
[05:26] Sara: any competitors we're worried about? procurement is seeing an AltServe AI pitch with cheaper baseline but no private VPC option.
[05:34] Maya: yep AltServe tends to be cheaper on meter but lacks dedicated private onprem with KMS + HSM. BigCloud Endpoints is doing marketplace bundles but vendor lock is a question. we'll include a quick comparison doc.
[05:45] Priya: timeline check — executive sign-off is 2028-05-08. we need to present cost scenarios and an operational plan.
[05:53] Maya: understood. we'll aim to deliver pricing + benchmark logs + SOC package by next Wednesday/Friday window. can we schedule the VPC scoping workshop for week of 2028-05-06?
[06:02] Priya: yes that works. Liam will host the internal session and invite ops.
[06:08] Liam: noted.
[06:10] Sara: one last procurement note — if we go to a 24-month committed term do you offer price protections or step-downs?
[06:17] Maya: yes, longer commitments get better unit pricing and a tiered discount schedule; i'll include 12mo vs 24mo pricing in the sheet and a clause for mid-term capacity re-eval.
[06:28] Priya: and for the pilot handoff, we'd like a checklist: security sign-off, perf bench, SSO/SAML test, canary run.
[06:36] Diego: we'll supply that checklist and a runbook for canary/A-B rollouts.
[06:40] Maya: perfect. quick recap: action items — Maya share commercial amendment and pricing scenarios (12/24 month), include cost vs latency; Diego run dedicated p99 bench + paste config; Diego send runbook + recommended RAG config; Redwood send SOC2/KMS docs; Valora to confirm procurement timeline and provide data flow doc.
[06:58] Priya: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side?
[07:02] Diego: no blockers, just need access for benching and a sample workload.
[07:07] Maya: i'll follow up in email with links and next meeting invite. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
